aj: seeing a regression on nightly between the soft-evict TTL change and kernel selection fallback. GPU OOMs spiked during the 03:00 batch window, curious if it's cache warmup related or a batching path that picks slower kernels which increase mem pressure :thinking:

maria: can you paste the perf dump? I want to see kernel + batch size distribution across requests.

aj: pasted below — this is from the 03:12 surge. note the huge rise in prefill/sec and a drop in prefix hit_rate.

maria: ```
PROFILE: 2026-03-14T03:12:11Z kernel=matmul_opt2 batch=48 latency_p50=14.2ms latency_p95=48.3ms mem_peak=4.1GB
PROFILE: 2026-03-14T03:12:15Z kernel=matmul_fallback batch=64 latency_p50=26.9ms latency_p95=90.4ms mem_peak=6.8GB
KV_CACHE: total_entries=1_120_431 hit_rate=0.53 prefill_rate=78/s frag_ratio=0.18
TTL_EVENTS: soft_evictions=4200 hard_evictions=12 ghost_hits=2
```

aj: we had the soft-evict TTL ramped from 60->300s for recent prefixes to reduce churn. hypothesis: longer TTL kept stale large prefixes in GPU slab and increased fragmentation, causing fallback kernels for large batches.

samir: interesting — fallback to matmul_fallback correlating with mem_peak jump. Fallback chosen when slab fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation for optimized kernel workspace. longer TTL means fewer evictions -> higher fragmentation over time.

kevin: also noticed a change in key canonicalization that landed last week: `prefix_key_v2`. It altered hashing for some long prompts; could change co-location of keys across slabs which affects fragmentation patterns.

lina: I pulled hit-rate traces by cohort. hot cohort hit_rate stayed ~0.92, but medium cohort dropped from 0.68 -> 0.53 during the window. cold cohort unchanged. So warmup for medium prefixes didn't happen. aggregation: medium prefixes account for 28% of tokens at spike.

aj: proposed quick experiment: revert TTL ramp for medium cohort to 90s, maintain hot at 3600s, enable ghost-window=30s to track evicted keys without immediate re-prefill. Also throttle prefill bursts above 60/s so we don't oversubscribe kernel queue. config below.

aj: ```
cache:
  ttl_policy: cohort_adaptive
  cohorts:
    hot: { ttl: 3600 }
    medium: { ttl: 90 }
    cold: { ttl: 30 }
  soft_eviction: true
  ghost_window_seconds: 30
prefill:
  max_burst_per_sec: 60
  smoothing_window_ms: 200
kernel_selection:
  max_batch_per_kernel: 64
  prefer_contig_alloc: true
```

maria: i ran a local sim with synthetic load matching medium-cohort shape. when medium_ttl=90s fragmentation metric (frag_ratio) dropped from 0.18 -> 0.07 after 15min; matmul_fallback events dropped 73%.

kevin: great. two more notes: 1) batching heuristic uses `latency_budget_ms` that we usually set to 30ms for interactive paths; during surge latency_budget was bumped to 100ms because of SLO experiments which allowed larger batches into optimized kernels — but if fragmentation prevents contig alloc, larger batches end up on fallback and amplify mem use. 2) we should consider adaptive batch cap derived from contiguous_slot_estimate instead of static cap.

samir: agree on contig estimate. propose: kernel scheduler queries a cheap slab-allocator probe: `can_allocate_contig(batch_slots)` and reduces batch if false. cheap probe cost ~0.2ms which is acceptable compared to fallback cost.

lina: i can add metrics for `contig_probe_success_rate` and an alert when success_rate < 0.85 for >2min. gives early warning before OOM.

aj: action items: @maria revert medium_ttl to 90s in canary (eng-runtime/canary-3), enable ghost_window and prefill throttling; @kevin draft scheduler change to `contig_probe` + adaptive_batch_cap; @lina add contig_probe metric and dashboard. I'll watch memory and prefill_rate.

maria: starting canary now. dev-bot: rolling deploy to eng-runtime/canary-3 (image: runtime:release-2026-03-14-rc2) :rocket:


dev-bot: deploy started by maria to eng-runtime/canary-3 at 2026-03-14T04:05:02Z

kevin: quick note — if we do probe per batch, ensure we cache contiguous estimate for ~100ms per worker to avoid probe storms.

samir: also adding a low-cost compaction path: when frag_ratio > 0.12, trigger background compaction that tries to coalesce small free slots on GPU between low-load windows. cheap version uses pinned buffer shuffles, estimated 0.5% throughput hit.

lina: will add compaction-related metrics: compaction_runs, compaction_time_ms, compaction_failure_rate.

aj: timeline: canary run for 30m, if matmul_fallback events drop and frag_ratio <0.1 we promote. otherwise rollback. will post summary in 30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: update 04:36Z — after 18m canary: prefill_rate down 42%, medium hit_rate up to 0.70, frag_ratio 0.08, matmul_fallback events down 68%. memory headroom improved ~1.8GB average.

aj: excellent. moving to staged rollout with prefill throttling enabled across all regions. kevin/samir, please prioritize the contig_probe + compaction follow-ups for next sprint.

kevin: ack. I'll open a PR for probe caching and adaptive batch cap today.

samir: i'll prototype compaction path and run perf sim.

lina: putting dashboards + alert on pager at 0.7 threshold.

aj: closing thread when PRs are linked. final note: this was an interaction between TTL policy + key hashing change + batching budget. reminds us to run end-to-end sim of cache+kernel interactions before TTL changes. we should add a checklist item for TTL adjustments: impact on fragmentation + contiguous allocation.

maria: agreed — adding a checklist item to infra runbook. good catch everyone.
